## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Blank for anonymity. The instructions do not say whether review is anonymous (copy dated 2026-03-24); the Press's authors'-rights page mentions blind review only conditionally ("if the journal uses an anonymous (blind) peer review system", copy dated 2024-01-18). What the instructions do say: all major articles undergo the "CA ☆ treatment": commentators selected from around the world write critiques that appear in the same issue, with a reply from the author; authors may choose at submission to have a major article considered with or without commentaries; authors may suggest and oppose reviewers (https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. Not stated on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Not stated. Commentaries by invited commentators are published with the article, per the instructions (copy dated 2026-03-24); that is a different thing from reviewer reports |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. Not stated. The revised-manuscript instructions say authors include responses to reviewers in the cover letter (copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. Not stated. The Press says decisions are the editors' responsibility "following rigorous, fair, and timely peer review" (https://web.archive.org/web/20250725184919/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/publication-ethics-statement, copy dated 2025-07-25) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a section on the journal's instructions page plus a separate page "Use of artificial intelligence tools" (https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/use-of-artificial-intelligence-tools), read in a real browser 2026-11-24 (curl had returned 403) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate: use is permitted with citation (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (permitted with a required citation, but images excluded; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Live page, read in a real browser 2026-11-24: editorial side, the journal does not use generative AI for editorial decisions, manuscript evaluation or correspondence, and may use validated AI-detection tools. Author side: permitted uses include generative AI with LLMs, readability editing, translation, transcription, literature-review and coding tools; AI-generated images are not accepted; AI cannot be credited as an author; authors stay responsible for originality, accuracy and integrity. Any AI use must be cited in two places: the Methods section and an "AI Tools" subsection inside the References Cited. Authors must give tool names and versions with the date range of use, the tasks performed, the extent of AI involvement and how human oversight and verification was done (the instructions page, Wayback copy dated 2026-03-24, gives the shorter version above) |

### Preprint Policy

> Press-level policy, applied to this journal; source: https://web.archive.org/web/20240118110836/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/jrnl_rights (Guidelines for Journal Authors' Rights, copy dated 2024-01-18, last updated 2021-08-02 per the page) and the instructions page copy dated 2026-03-24. Journal-specific preprint wording was not found.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes, with a caution | The Press says authors may deposit pre- and post-acceptance versions to a repository or preprint/working-paper service, and encourages consulting the editor before posting a paper intended for submission, because posting can compromise anonymous review and can count as prior publication; authors should disclose any prior posting to the editor |
| Under review | Blank | The authors'-rights page covers the "submitted manuscript" version as a pre-acceptance version; no rule for posting during review beyond the caution above. The instructions say the journal will not consider anything published before "in any form or language" and does not consider more than one submission at a time per author |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes | Accepted manuscript may be deposited in a non-commercial repository with a 12-month post-publication embargo on public availability (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, open access policy section). Embargo: 12 months |
| Version of Record | Blank | Published PDF may be deposited in the same way under the 12-month embargo (same section); gold open access articles are published under CC BY-NC |

## Format

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Major articles; reports; literary ethnographic manuscripts; short manuscripts accompanied by translations; visual essays; discussion items; reviews by invitation only. Forums and CA+ electronic enhancements are mentioned (https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct, copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Word limit** | Major articles 6,000 to 10,000 words with references and endnotes counted, up to 12 figures and tables; manuscripts over 10,000 words are returned without review. Reports 3,000 to 5,000 words, up to 4 figures and tables; over 5,000 returned without review. Literary ethnographic manuscripts under 5,000 words. Short manuscripts with translation: English version under 5,000 words. Visual essays: exegetical essay of 2,000 to 3,000 words with 1 to 5 images. Discussion items up to 800 words including references; they respond to publications from the previous 8 months (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24). An older checklist copy (dated 2025-01-26, https://web.archive.org/web/20250126093512/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/checklist) gives different ceilings (major papers 12,000, forum papers 7,500); the instructions say they take precedence over other preparation material, and the later copy is the one used here |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Stated as firm for submission: over-length manuscripts are returned without review but "with encouragement for revision" (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24). No exceptions are described |
| **Abstract limit** | 200 words maximum for every format that needs one (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate limit; references and endnotes count toward the word limits above. CA reference style per the CA Style Guide (https://web.archive.org/web/20210418153155/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/style, copy dated 2021-04-18); English only |
| **Supplementary material** | Electronic enhancements ("CA+" papers) such as sound, video, extra data or maps are welcomed if the editor approves; the journal offers to publish a final version of an accepted manuscript in its original language as an online supplement on request (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | Major articles up to 12 figures and tables; reports, literary ethnographic and short manuscripts up to 4; visual essays 1 to 5 images (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24). Figures must be TIFF or EPS, not JPEG or GIF; Word or RTF manuscript, double spaced, 12-point |

### Orientation

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Both appear. Among the 311 OpenAlex articles of 2021 to 2026 that have an abstract: "ethnograph-" in 95 (30.6%), theory words in 58 (18.7%), archaeology words in 54 (17.4%); regexes in Methodological Preferences. Major articles must make theoretical or methodological interventions in anthropology broadly construed (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Qualitative and interpretive work is more frequent by keyword: quantitative or statistical terms in 7 of 311 (2.3%) and "survey" in 4 (1.3%), against "ethnograph-" 95 (30.6%) and "fieldwork" 39 (12.5%) (OpenAlex abstracts, counted 2026-11-23). Biological terms appear in 16 (5.1%), so the quantitative share is probably under-represented by these words alone |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The journal states a "comprehensive view of anthropology" covering all scholarship on human cultures and on the human or closely related species, and expects articles to be read by scholars and students across the four fields (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24). In the abstract sample: archaeology 54 (17.4%), linguistic 16 (5.1%), biological 16 (5.1%) |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex works for this source dated 2021 to 2026 (483 records, of which 333 are of type article and 311 of those have an abstract = 93.4%; retrieved 2026-11-23; counts use the abstract-bearing articles as denominator; OpenAlex-derived counts in this entry were not independently re-run at the verification pass); Wayback copies of the journal's board and instructions pages. Keyword regexes are in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics. Crossref holds no abstracts for this journal (0 of 489 records), so Crossref is not used for counts.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | The journal's own statements: established "to create a worldwide community of scholars that transcends national borders and parochial intellectual orientations"; commentators "selected from around the world"; articles in English only, with an optional online supplement in the original language and a format for short manuscripts accompanied by a translation into the field-site language (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct). Author-country counts could not be derived: OpenAlex carries a country for only 51 of 333 articles of this source |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 59 editorial-board entries on the live board page (https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/board, read in a real browser 2026-11-24; the Wayback copy dated 2026-03-22 held 53), counted by the country printed in each entry: United States 23, Australia 7, UK 4, Brazil 3, Germany 2, Canada 2, China 2, Mexico 2, and one each in Argentina, Austria, French Polynesia, Hong Kong (printed "HK"), India, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Norway, Scotland (printed as such), Singapore, South Africa, Sweden and Turkey (23+7+4+3 = 37; 4 x 2 = 8; 14 x 1 = 14; 37+8+14 = 59). The two editors are both in Australia |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Keyword counts in 311 abstracts: "indigenous" 30 (9.6%); colonial, decolonial or settler terms 37 (11.9%); religion terms 29 (9.3%). The journal accepts "literary ethnographic" writing that departs from conventional article format and visual essays (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Counts in 311 abstracts: gender and sexuality terms 38 (12.2%); race and racism terms 13 (4.2%); see Sensitive Topics for regexes. No editorial statement on these topics was read; the editorial "To the Readers of Current Anthropology" by the new editors (Current Anthropology 66(3), June 2025, https://doi.org/10.1086/735733) could not be read because it is behind access control |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No school is named by the journal; it states a commitment to "a comprehensive view of anthropology" and critique as the means to it (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24). Most-cited articles dated 2021 to 2026 in OpenAlex (retrieved 2026-11-23): "An Imagined Past? Nomadic Narratives in Central Asian Archaeology" (https://doi.org/10.1086/714245, 115 citations); "Magic, Explanations, and Evil: The Origins and Design of Witches and Sorcerers" (https://doi.org/10.1086/713111, 81); "Predigestion as an Evolutionary Impetus for Human Use of Fermented Food" (https://doi.org/10.1086/715238, 66); "Of Plots and Men: The Heuristics of Conspiracy Theories" (https://doi.org/10.1086/713829, 65); "Evolution without Inheritance: Steps to an Ecology of Learning" (https://doi.org/10.1086/722437, 53). The list mixes archaeology, evolutionary and cognitive anthropology and sociocultural theory; it is a citation list, not an editorial position |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Major articles must make theoretical or methodological interventions into current research foci within anthropology, broadly construed, provide strong synthetic foundations and be written for readers across the four fields; reports must make the significance for anthropology "writ large" clear in the text (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with the discipline as a whole rather than one subfield: the journal says it publishes research on humankind "in the broadest possible way" and treats active scholarly critique (commentary and reply) as central (same page). Literary ethnographic manuscripts are meant not to have extensive literature reviews, while still being grounded in research and scholarship (same page).
- **Article types and length**: major articles 6,000 to 10,000 words, reports 3,000 to 5,000, discussion items up to 800, visual essays 2,000 to 3,000 words of exegesis, all with references counted (same page, copy dated 2026-03-24).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: no open call for papers was found on the pages read. A menu entry for the Wenner-Gren Symposium Series exists (copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: over-length manuscripts are returned without review (same page). For out-of-scope manuscripts no source states a consequence, and no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev, 0 reviews: https://scirev.org/reviews/current-anthropology/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Method counts are over the 311 OpenAlex articles dated 2021 to 2026 that have an abstract (333 articles in all; https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:0011-3204,publication_year:2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23), matching title plus the abstract rebuilt from OpenAlex's inverted index, case-insensitive. In the regexes below, `\|` inside a table cell is a literal alternation bar `|` (escaped only because of the markdown table). Shares use 311 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written mainly for psychology and HCI; where a row does not fit anthropology the cell says so, and rows were added for fieldwork, archival, archaeological, biological, linguistic and visual work.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 (quantitative methods in general; no experiments counted) | Regex `\b(?:quantitative\|statistical\|statistics\|regression\|survey data)\b`: 7 of 311 (2.3%); regex `\bsurveys?\b`: 4 (1.3%). Experimental designs were not counted separately. Biological terms (regex `\b(?:genetic\|genomic\|ancient DNA\|isotop\w*\|skeletal\|bioarchaeolog\w*\|primate\w*)\b`) 16 (5.1%, which alone would score 3) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Regex `\binterview\w*`: 14 of 311 (4.5%); `\bqualitative\b`: 4 (1.3%). The row fits poorly: the dominant qualitative mode is ethnography, not named interviews (next row) |
| Ethnography / fieldwork (added row) | 3 | Regex `\bethnograph\w*`: 95 of 311 (30.6%); regex `\bfield-?work\b\|\bfield research\b`: 39 (12.5%); `\bparticipant[- ]observation\b`: 3 (1.0%, score 1 on its own). The instructions also invite literary ethnographic manuscripts and say they must meet "the highest standards for research ethics and fieldwork practice" (copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| Autoethnography | 1 | Regex `\bauto-?ethnograph\w*`: 2 of 311 (0.6%) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Regex `\btheor(?:y\|ies\|etical\|ize\|izing\|izations?)\b`: 58 of 311 (18.6%). The instructions ask major articles for theoretical or methodological interventions (copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| Archival / historical (added row) | 2 | Regex `\barchiv(?:e\|es\|al)\b`: 9 of 311 (2.9%) gives the score. Regex `\bhistor(?:y\|ies\|ical)\b` matches 80 (25.7%, which would score 3), but history words also mark topics rather than methods, so it is not used for the score |
| Archaeological (added row) | 3 | Regex `\barchaeolog\w*\|\barcheolog\w*`: 54 of 311 (17.4%); 17 of all 333 article titles match |
| Biological / evolutionary (added row) | 3 | Biological regex above: 16 of 311 (5.1%); "Predigestion as an Evolutionary Impetus..." is among the most cited (https://doi.org/10.1086/715238) |
| Linguistic (added row) | 3 | Regex `\blinguistic\b\|\blanguage ideolog\w*\|\bsociolinguistic\w*`: 16 of 311 (5.1%) |
| Multimodal / visual (added row) | 3 | Regex `\b(?:multimodal\|film\|video\|podcast\|photograph\w*\|visual)\b`: 25 of 311 (8.0%). The journal has a visual essay format and visual media editors (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24; board copy dated 2026-03-22) |
| Mixed methods | 1 | Regex `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b`: 1 of 311 (0.3%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 1 | Regex `\bmeta-?analy\w*\|\bsystematic review\b`: 1 of 311 (0.3%). The row does not fit the field's usual forms |

### Voice & Style

|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Count: of the 311 OpenAlex abstracts of 2021 to 2026, 220 (70.7%) contain a first-person pronoun by regex `\b(?:I\|my\|me\|we\|our\|us)\b` (case-sensitive; plural "we" and "our" can be a co-author team or generic; OpenAlex, counted 2026-11-23). Examples among the latest-indexed abstracts: "I argue" (https://doi.org/10.1086/743068), "I present and theorize" (https://doi.org/10.1086/742929), "we explore" (https://doi.org/10.1086/742838), "we present ethnographic data" (https://doi.org/10.1086/743006). The instructions give no rule on first person |
| **Expected density** | Major articles 6,000 to 10,000 words including references and endnotes; reports 3,000 to 5,000 (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct). 230 of the 333 articles (69.1%) have one author, 49 two, 19 three and 35 four or more (OpenAlex authorship lists, counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of at most 200 words for major articles, reports, literary ethnographic manuscripts, short manuscripts and visual essays; no keyword requirement was seen in the instructions (copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Writing style notes** | Articles are expected to be read across anthropology's four fields (same page). Manuscript: Word or RTF, double spaced, 12-point, numbered pages, endnotes at the end, a separate cover letter file, references in CA style per the CA Style Guide; English only; figures as TIFF or EPS (same page; style guide copy dated 2021-04-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20210418153155/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/style) |
| **Authorship pattern** | See Expected density: 69.1% single-author among all 333 articles (OpenAlex, 2026-11-23). The instructions say the journal does not consider more than one submission at a time for any author, with co-authored cases handled individually |

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |

| **Dominant tradition** | The board page does not label members by subfield, so no per-subfield count is given. Affiliations printed include universities and a few other bodies (for example "British Institute in Eastern Africa", "Sharma Centre for Heritage Education", "CONICET/Universidad de San Martin" and "Max Planck"). The 2 editors are both at the Australian National University; the reviews editor is in the United States | https://web.archive.org/web/20260322070351/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/board (copy dated 2026-03-22) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The instructions state no general ethics-approval or consent rule (searched the saved page text for "IRB", "consent" and "ethics approval": not present); they say literary ethnographic manuscripts and visual essays "should conform to the highest standards for research ethics" and practice (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct). The Press statement requires authors to warrant originality and to give conflict-of-interest and funding disclosures (https://web.archive.org/web/20250725184919/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/publication-ethics-statement, copy dated 2025-07-25) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the majority: 230 of 333 articles (69.1%) in OpenAlex for 2021 to 2026 (counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No independent-scholar rule on the pages read. Board entries include non-university affiliations such as a heritage-education centre and a research institute in the board copy dated 2026-03-22 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260322070351/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/board); the instructions ask for authors' affiliations on the title-page information entered at submission (copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | None stated on the instructions page (searched the saved text for "data availability" and "data sharing": not present); data sets may be submitted as part of electronic enhancements if the editor approves (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Unclear: anonymity of review is not stated (see Peer Review). The submission needs a cover letter and title-page information typed into the system, and the Press cautions that posting a manuscript can compromise anonymous review where used (authors'-rights copy dated 2024-01-18, https://web.archive.org/web/20240118110836/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/jrnl_rights) |
| **AI use** | Permitted but must be cited; no AI for images; AI cannot be an author (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24); see AI Policy |
| **Open access and cost** | Green open access free with a 12-month embargo; gold open access USD 1,500 under CC BY-NC (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24, https://web.archive.org/web/20260324073041/https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/ca/instruct) |
| **Copyright** | Copyright for major articles, reports, forums, discussion items and commentaries is assigned to the Wenner-Gren Foundation; other contributions stay with their authors, with a non-exclusive licence to the journal (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |
| **Single-submission rule** | The journal does not consider more than one submission at a time from any author, with co-authored cases decided case by case (instructions copy dated 2026-03-24) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: major articles over 10,000 words and reports over 5,000 words are returned without review; references and endnotes count (Format; instructions copy dated 2026-03-24).
- **One manuscript at a time**: the journal does not consider more than one submission at a time from any author (Practical Concerns; same page).
- **Prior publication**: contributions already published in any form or language are not considered (Preprint Policy; same page). The Press adds that posting a paper can count as prior publication, so the editor should be consulted first (authors'-rights copy dated 2024-01-18).
- **English only**: articles are published in English only; a supplement in the original language is possible on request (Format; same page).
- **AI use**: use without citation, or AI-generated images, falls outside the stated policy (AI Policy; same page).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read. The live instructions page (real browser 2026-11-24) contains no anonymisation, blind-review or referee wording (0 hits for those words), so no anonymity requirement is stated there.

### Soft Tax

- **Commentary route**: major articles are by default considered with invited commentaries and an author reply, and the journal says an article without commentaries "will likely follow a faster publication timeline" (Peer Review, Review Cycle Time). Choosing the route is part of the submission; no durations are published.
- **Open access cost**: gold open access is USD 1,500, with an additional unstated fee for a CC BY licence; green deposit has a 12-month embargo (Open Access, Preprint Policy).
- **Copyright assignment**: copyright for major articles and reports goes to the Wenner-Gren Foundation (Practical Concerns), which may matter to authors with funder licence requirements.
- **Format work**: figures must be TIFF or EPS and the manuscript Word or RTF with a separate cover letter (Format).

### Best Suited For

- Syntheses that make a theoretical or methodological intervention readable across anthropology's four fields: the instructions require this of major articles (Framing Requirements).
- Archaeological, evolutionary and biological work alongside sociocultural work: archaeology 17.4%, biological 5.1%, ethnography 30.6% of 311 abstracts, and the most-cited recent articles are archaeological, evolutionary and cognitive (Orientation, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Experimental forms: literary ethnography, visual essays and short manuscripts with translation are listed formats (Format).
- Shorter pieces: reports of 3,000 to 5,000 words and discussion items of up to 800 words responding to recent publications (Format).
- Authors comfortable with open critique: major articles are published with commentaries and a reply unless the author opts out at submission (Peer Review).

### Not Recommended For

- Articles that need more than 10,000 words including references (Hard Blockers).
- Authors who need a published turnaround time: none is given (Review Cycle Time).
- Single-subfield technical work with no argument for readers beyond it: the instructions expect cross-field readability and a synthetic foundation (Framing Requirements). This follows from the stated aim, not from any reported rejection.
- Authors who cannot assign copyright for major articles to the foundation (Practical Concerns).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [American Anthropologist](american-anthropologist.md) | Another broad four-field venue; its entry records an 8,000-word limit with references counted and an author-anonymised review model, so a CA manuscript within 8,000 words needs little cutting; check the entry's scope and submission-platform notes first |
| 2 | [Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute](journal-of-the-royal-anthropological-institute.md) | A society journal for social anthropology from the United Kingdom; its entry records its own limits, which should be checked before choosing |
| 3 | American Ethnologist (Wiley; no entry in this corpus) | Not read; named only because it appears on the same Google Scholar Metrics Anthropology list (rank 15, h5-index 22; https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=top_venues&hl=en&vq=soc_anthropology, fetched 2026-11-23) |
